From: Bryan Hall <bryan.hall@acmecorp.com>

Cc: Tanya Ortiz <tanya.ortiz@acmecorp.com>, legal@acmecorp.com

Subject: MSA Redlines: Damages exclusions (draft)

Hi Olga — attaching our suggested MSA redline (see attachment). A few points on damages: we are proposing a mutual exclusion for consequential, incidental, special, punitive and exemplary damages, but with standard carve-outs. Please review and confirm Redwood's comfort with the following carve-outs to the exclusion:

- Exceptions: liability for (i) willful misconduct; (ii) gross negligence; (iii) breach of confidentiality or unauthorized access to Customer Data; and (iv) Customer's indemnified claims.
- Cap: liability to be limited to the greater of: (a) fees paid in the prior 12 months; or (b) USD 1,000,000.

Two questions for you up front: is Redwood prepared to accept a mutual exclusion or do you prefer a one-way exclusion in our favor? Also, Acme wants explicit language that excludes consequential damages but preserves liability for data breaches and indemnity claims.

Attachment(s): ACME_MSA_redline.docx

Best,
Bryan
Counsel, Acme Corporation

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-25T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MSA Redlines: Damages exclusions (draft) — need legal position and playbook

Marcus / Laura — forwarding Bryan's redline from Acme. Two negotiation axes here:

1) Mutual vs one-way exclusion: Acme has proposed mutual (both sides cannot recover consequential damages). Sales appetite: we prefer one-way (customer cannot recover consequential from Redwood) because it reduces risk, but that will be a sticking point at enterprise legal review.
2) Carve-outs and definitions: Acme wants to preserve data-breach, indemnity, willful misconduct. We need firm guidance on: (a) whether "data breach" should be an exception to the exclusion or treated under indemnity/limited cap; (b) whether to accept their cap formula (12 months fees or $1M).

Requests:
- Laura: recommended default language (mutual vs one-way) and a short script for Marcus if Acme asks about why we need a one-way carve.
- Marcus: any commercial constraints on cap amounts (is finance ok with 12 months)?

I attached our standard seller-friendly redline from our playbook earlier this year — it proposes a one-way exclusion but preserves carve-outs for privacy incidents and IP indemnity.

Thanks —
Olga
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-26T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA Redlines: Damages exclusions (draft) — comments and recommended redline

Olga / Marcus — read Bryan's draft and our playbook. Legal position below (short version first, suggested redline after).

Recommendation (short): Aim for a mutual exclusion as a commercial compromise unless the customer is higher risk. If we can get the cap to 12 months' fees and carve out: (i) Customer Data breaches (expressly defined); (ii) Customer indemnified claims (IP/infringement); (iii) gross negligence or willful misconduct — that's acceptable. Keep the cap formula and add a negotiated uplift path for enterprise (Finance: 12 months is standard; Marcus, confirm if we need $1M floor).

Key draftingnotes:
- Define "Consequential Damages" rather than listing — but keep examples (loss of profits, business interruption).
- For data breaches, use a narrow definition: "unauthorized access or disclosure of Customer Data resulting from Seller's failure to comply with its security obligations." That should remain outside the exclusion.
- Carve out indemnity obligations (IP/tort claims) from both the exclusion and the cap.
- One-way vs mutual: if Acme insists on mutual, it's reasonable. A one-way exclusion in our favor is stronger but will likely lead to protracted negotiation; pick fights only if revenue justifies.

Suggested redline (language you can paste into the doc):
"Limitation of Liability. Except for liability arising from (a) a party's willful misconduct or gross negligence; (b) breach of confidentiality obligations with respect to Customer Data; (c) Seller's indemnification obligations for third-party intellectual property infringement; and (d) fraud, neither party shall be liable for any special, incidental, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages (including lost profits, loss of business, or loss of use), whether in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability or otherwise. EXCEPT FOR THE FOREGOING, THE AGGREGATE LIABILITY OF SELLER ARISING OUT OF OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (I) ALL FEES PAID BY CUSTOMER TO SELLER IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO LIABILITY, OR (II) ONE MILLION DOLLARS (US$1,000,000)."

Operational notes for Marcus: if Acme pushes for one-way mutuality, propose mutual but ask for a carve-out that preserves the cap for Seller liability tied to data breaches (i.e., treat breaches as outside the cap only where caused by Seller's gross negligence or willful misconduct). If procurement presses on floor amounts, Finance prefers to keep the 12-month formula and $1M floor unless there's strong commercial justification for a higher cap.

Attachments: suggested redline text file (I've pasted language above so you can copy).

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Bryan — thanks for the redline and the quick turnaround. Forwarding our internal counsel's recommended compromise below and proposing three points to accelerate:

1) Mutual exclusion is acceptable as a compromise. Our counsel suggests the language below which keeps consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages excluded for both sides but with narrow, express carve-outs (willful misconduct/gross negligence, breach of confidentiality re: Customer Data, and IP indemnity).
2) Cap formula: we can accept the 12-months or $1M floor. Finance has flagged the $1M floor as a reasonable backstop for early-year volumes.
3) Definitions: we propose a short definition for "Customer Data breach" tied to Seller's failure to meet security obligations — we'd like to preserve remedies for regulatory notification costs and direct remediation.

Proposed language (please consider adding to your redline under Section X):
[Paste Laura's language here — see attached for machine copy so you can insert cleanly into track changes]

If Acme is comfortable with mutual + the carve-outs above, we think the rest of the draft MSA should be straightforward. If you prefer Redwood to keep a one-way exclusion, we can explain commercially why that limits Redwood's tail risk — happy to discuss on a quick call.

Best,
